content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge treats Matthew 1:16's two possible readings as the reason for UNDERDETERMINED, which is exactly the kind of two-sense-verse treatment K-S2 governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. I weighed whether this forbids any UNDERDETERMINED finding where a verse admits two readings, against whether it only forbids treating a two-sense verse as unsettled while preserving both senses.","why":"The judge's stated ground is that Matthew 1:16 admits both readings, so it treats a two-sense verse as open and underdetermined instead of letting both senses stand."}
